incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and PHP-based web infrastructure worldwide
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited two critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell') against internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces, aided by the appliances' lack of address space layout randomization support.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Networks confirmed successful exploitation against PAN-OS devices and set the exploit maturity rating to 'attack'; Censys reports more than 10 million of 42 million exposed PHP instances have been patched so far, with millions more on end-of-life branches that will never receive a fix.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a test environment to gain access to university systems.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to more than 525,000 people was stolen.

incidents.victim: Keystone (cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker) and its customers
incidents.vector: A hacker stole Keystone's device authentication key, which is written to each wallet during assembly, cannot be changed, and is used to verify device authenticity.
incidents.impact: Keystone is destroying nearly 19,000 affected devices and has suspended all wallet deliveries, warning the stolen key could be used to produce counterfeit wallets containing backdoors.

incidents.victim: Andromeda (cloud AI platform) and its customers
incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to customer accounts on the Andromeda cloud AI platform as part of a broader, industry-wide campaign targeting AI infrastructure providers.
incidents.impact: Customer credentials and AI API keys were stolen; compromised accounts and infrastructure access have reportedly been rented out on underground forums.

incidents.vector: A hacker gained access to internal business systems via a learning management system and a customer relationship management platform.
incidents.impact: Genesys said it found no evidence the attacker pivoted to its public customer clouds.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an internal CRM platform used by business partners to sell energy contracts.
incidents.impact: ENGIE is notifying affected customers of its French gas supply business about the security breach.

incidents.vector: Threat actors used an infinite mint exploit to create and steal newly minted tokens from the Initia crypto project.
incidents.impact: Approximately $2.7 million worth of tokens were created and stolen.

incidents.vector: A suspected Brazilian hacking group breached Convertr via the Plausible open-source analytics platform and deployed a credit-card skimmer through its analytics script.
incidents.impact: Customer payment card data was likely harvested; the group is a known Magecart-style threat actor active since 2024.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Node.js, Python, .NET, PHP (Windows builds) and other software bundling the Brotli library; Adobe Commerce/Magento merchants
incidents.vector: A buffer-overflow flaw in the widely used Brotli decompression library (CVE-2026-111497, 'Node2Shell') enables unauthenticated remote code execution when vulnerable software decompresses attacker-supplied data; separately, CISA confirmed active exploitation of an unrestricted file-upload flaw in Adobe Commerce/Magento (CVE-2026-48356).
incidents.impact: CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; Wiz found 91% of cloud environments contain Brotli-vulnerable resources, prompting emergency patches from Microsoft, Node.js, PHP, and others.

incidents.victim: Multiple Hive and Nefilim ransomware victims (hospitals, law firms, government entities, businesses — approximately 1,500 organizations worldwide, 2018-2023)
incidents.vector: As an affiliate of the Hive and Nefilim ransomware operations, the defendant deployed ransomware against victims including hospitals, law firms, and a dentist's office, encrypting data and issuing extortion demands.
incidents.impact: Artem Stryzhak, a Ukrainian national, was sentenced to 70 months in prison; the combined Hive/Nefilim conspiracies caused more than $100 million in losses. Co-conspirator Volodymyr Tymoshchuk remains a fugitive, with an $11 million reward offered for information leading to his arrest.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System
incidents.vector: A ransomware gang calling itself 'BYOD' breached the health system's network; the specific initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The hospital diverted ambulances for about two hours, suspended outpatient surgeries, and canceled medical school classes for two days; attackers claim to have compromised 36,000 machines and stolen data on students, patients, and employees. A similarly disruptive cyberattack also hit University Hospitals in Ohio around the same time.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an unauthenticated, internet-exposed logging service to breach government networks and exfiltrate data before being detected and evicted.
incidents.impact: Officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks after attackers stole highly sensitive data on roughly 750,000 citizens — about a third of Moldova's population — including family, financial, health, and identity details; this is the second major breach of Moldovan government systems this year.

incidents.victim: Vanden Broele (Belgian government software supplier) and 120+ Belgian local authorities
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Vanden Broele's eSignFlow document-signing platform, a system widely used by Belgian local governments.
incidents.impact: The company took systems offline to prevent abuse; more than 120 local authorities were reportedly affected.

incidents.victim: Warp (cloud platform) and an infrastructure supplier
incidents.vector: Intruders used a swarm of AI agents to breach one of Warp's infrastructure suppliers.
incidents.impact: Agent trace and telemetry data was stolen for roughly 1% of Warp's customers.

incidents.victim: Organizations and users relying on eMudhra-issued TLS and code-signing certificates
incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 key-generation process produced eight intermediate CA private keys with only 3-8 bits of effective entropy instead of 384, making them trivially recoverable and allowing anyone to forge trusted TLS or code-signing certificates.
incidents.impact: Microsoft, Apple, Google, and Mozilla blocked or revoked the affected eMudhra intermediates; Microsoft shipped an out-of-band Windows update and removed seven certificates from the Windows and Edge trust lists, while many command-line tools and Linux/Python certificate stores remain exposed until updated.

incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member-information-retrieval API to extract customer records in bulk.
incidents.impact: Approximately 22.5 million customer records were compromised, including email addresses, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and employment information.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack hit IDCFrontier's cloud hosting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted services for 495 downstream companies and local governments that relied on IDCFrontier's cloud platform.
